research: New Mexico is 7-1, 4-0 in the Mountain West and No. 22 in the AP poll, its first ranking in school history (Predictem, Nov 3). Context only, already priced.
New Mexico leads FBS in scoring defense (11.9 ppg), is No. 1 in success rate allowed and leads the nation in turnover margin (+17), with 17 INTs (Predictem Nov 3; WagerTalk Nov 4). Helps New Mexico.

[angle] Nevada has 3 takeaways all season, fewest in FBS, against a Lobos QB (Toa Fa'avae) with 1 TD and 6 INTs over his last three games, 3 of them at San Jose State. Nevada's defense has rarely turned that kind of QB play into turnovers, which helps New Mexico (Predictem Nov 3; WagerTalk Nov 4).

New Mexico has scored exactly 21 points in each of its last three games (21-16 over NDSU and San Jose State) and needed extra time to beat two-win Hawaii. A stalled offense makes a double-digit margin harder, which helps Nevada (WagerTalk, Nov 4).

[angle] Nevada QB situation: starter Carter Jones (arm) has missed three straight games and his status is unclear. With Jones, Nevada averaged 33 ppg and 219.8 rushing yards; without him, 13 ppg and 114.3. His status swings this spread (Predictem, Nov 3).

In Nevada's last game, a 27-0 loss at UCLA, Luke Duncan threw three INTs in the first 7:27 and AJ Bianco (now hurt, ankle) replaced him: four INTs in all. Helps New Mexico if a backup starts (Predictem Nov 3; WagerTalk Nov 4).

Nevada's defense is respectable: 21.8 ppg allowed, 23rd in yards per play allowed, held UCLA to 303 yards; DE Dylan LaBarbera has 4.5 sacks. Helps Nevada stay inside the number (Predictem; WagerTalk).

Line: New Mexico opened -12.5 and fell to -9.5, with Nevada at 94-100% of the money per WagerTalk (Nov 4). The archive closes it at -10.5, back up a point from midweek. Slate -9.5. Treated as fair, not a reason.
Total fell from 42.5-43.5 to 36.5-38.5 midweek (closed 39.5). The market expects a low-scoring game. A low total isn't counted as a reason (lessons).
Covers showed 58% of picks on New Mexico ATS. Previews split: Predictem took NM -9.5 (26-10); WagerTalk/GoldSheet took Nevada +9.5 (21-13). Both are priced, not counted as reasons.
[angle] New Mexico has never won in Reno; last year's meeting went 24-22 to the Lobos. Old venue history is not weighed.
New Mexico's injury watch: C Kaden Robnett and WR Massiah Mingo. Nevada TE DJ Asiasi is out for the season (Predictem, Nov 3). Minor.
games.reasoning: New Mexico's elite defense and turnover edge against a Nevada offense scoring 13 a game without Carter Jones points to about a 10-point Lobos win. That is right on the 9.5 slate number. The Lobos' offense has stalled at 21 points three weeks running. The deciding fact, whether Jones plays, is unresolved in the sources, so this is a pass. A confirmed Jones return would have pushed me to Nevada; a confirmed third-string QB would have pushed me to New Mexico.

research: Arizona QB Noah Fifita averages 324 passing yards (6th nationally) with 19 TD and 4 INT. WR Isaiah Mizell has three straight 100-yard games (Predictem, Nov 3). Helps Arizona.
Arizona has averaged nearly 38 ppg over its last six games, is 4-0 at home and has won six straight in Tucson (WagerTalk Nov 4; Predictem Nov 3). Helps Arizona.

TCU's defense allows 14.1 ppg (8th in FBS) and 4.6 second-half ppg (2nd), leads the Big 12 in third-down defense, is 12th in opponent-adjusted pass defense (6.2 YPA) and hasn't allowed more than 21 to anyone (Predictem; WagerTalk). Helps TCU against Arizona's pass-first offense.

[angle] TCU's four losses are all one-score games (UNC 5, UCF 8, BYU 7, WVU 4), and its worst loss is 8 points. That is a repeated pattern of staying inside about 8 points (Predictem, Nov 3). Helps TCU +7.5.

TCU's offense is weak: 23.2 ppg (101st), about 19 without its games against Grambling and Arkansas State. QB Jaden Craig (Harvard transfer) has struggled, and TCU trailed Kansas 13-0 at half before winning 22-16 while being outgained by 150+ yards (WagerTalk; Predictem). Helps Arizona.

[angle] TCU fired its offensive line coach after the West Virginia loss, having allowed 20 sacks in seven games. Arizona has 25 sacks (10th nationally), though its own line allows 2.75 sacks a game (116th) (Predictem). Sacks cut both ways.

Arizona injuries: WR R.J. Mosley is out (a 'significant' injury per Brent Brennan) and Tre Spivey is out for the year. RB Kedrick Reescano averages 3.6 YPC, so the run game is weak (Predictem, Nov 3). Helps TCU.

[angle] Spot: Arizona comes off a 34-26 loss at Texas Tech on a late TD that dented its playoff hopes, and hosts Big 12 leader Utah next week. WagerTalk flags a possible hangover; it is also a look-ahead spot (WagerTalk, Nov 4). Mild TCU lean.
Line: Arizona opened -8.5/-9.5 midweek with 63-100% of the money on Arizona (WagerTalk Nov 4). Slate -7.5, archive close -6. The market moved toward TCU; the close is treated as fair, not a reason.
Previews split: WagerTalk took Arizona -9.5 (31-17); Predictem took TCU +8.5 (23-17). Priced, not counted.
Total about 42.5-44.5 midweek, closed 46.5. TCU hasn't played in Tucson since 2003.
TCU punter John Hoyet Chance has dropped half his punts inside the 20, which helps TCU's defense win field position (Predictem).
games.reasoning: This is Arizona's pass offense against an elite TCU pass and second-half defense, with a TCU offense that rarely scores more than 20. I project Arizona by about 7, half a point under the 7.5 slate number, which isn't a gap. TCU's string of one-score losses and Arizona's sandwich spot point mildly to TCU, but the market close of -6 already reflects it, so this is a pass. A healthy, efficient Arizona run game would have moved me to Arizona.
